items.headline: Cole Palmer keeps captaincy as Arsenal defensive triple targets Sunderland clean sheet
items.summary:
Cole Palmer remains captain for Gameweek 4, with his differential appeal over João Pedro strengthening the case despite Pedro's strong form. Erling Haaland is untouchable in the forward line and is already earmarked for the armband in Gameweek 5, when Manchester City host Sunderland.

The defence is heavily committed to Arsenal, with David Raya, Calafiori and Conso forming a triple-up aimed at Sunderland's visit. De Cuyper completes the back line and retains appeal because he is still operating at left wing, a role expected to continue until Kaoru Mitoma returns.

The early transfer is Rayan Cherki to Morgan Rogers, completed before Rogers rises to £7.6m. Cherki is not viewed as a poor asset, but concerns over his minutes make Rogers the more secure and attractive option both for this week and longer term. Dominik Szoboszlai is kept for Fulham's weak defence, while Gross also has a favourable Coventry fixture.

João Pedro is backed for Hull at home and beyond, while Yoane Wissa survives despite disappointing in Gameweek 3. Wissa's upcoming Hull home match in Gameweek 5 and Coventry away in Gameweek 6 offer enough fixture upside to justify patience rather than another immediate transfer.
key_points: Cole Palmer is the Gameweek 4 captain, with his lower ownership making him more appealing than João Pedro.
Erling Haaland is held without question and is planned as captain for Manchester City's Gameweek 5 home fixture against Sunderland.
David Raya, Calafiori and Conso make up an aggressive Arsenal defensive triple-up targeting a Sunderland clean sheet.
De Cuyper remains a useful pick while he continues to play at left wing until Mitoma returns.
Morgan Rogers replaces Rayan Cherki after a move made before Rogers reaches £7.6m, primarily because Cherki's minutes look unreliable.
Szoboszlai is retained for the Fulham fixture, while Gross is favoured against Coventry.
Wissa is kept despite his Gameweek 3 blank because Hull at home in Gameweek 5 and Coventry away in Gameweek 6 provide a favourable short-term run.

items.headline: Palmer dominates Gameweek 4 captaincy as elite managers pile into Chelsea attack
items.summary:
Cole Palmer is the overwhelming Gameweek 4 captaincy pick among leading FPL managers, backed by 72% despite Hull having kept three straight clean sheets. Chelsea’s attacking output makes the fixture hard to ignore: Palmer scores twice after coming off the bench in the cup, while Morgan Rogers records four assists in the same match and has returned in all three league gameweeks. João Pedro is the main alternative captain at 22%, with Erling Haaland, Bruno Fernandes, Rogers and Alexander Isak attracting only isolated support. Most triple-captain users back Palmer; one notable exception instead triples Isak against a Fulham side ranked 19th for expected goals conceded.

Rogers is the standout transfer target, bought by 64% of the top managers, with Palmer second and Arsenal budget defender Constant also heavily recruited after an impressive European debut at £4.4m. Palmer and Rogers are viewed as the priority buys for managers without Chelsea coverage, while João Pedro remains widely backed. Arsenal assets continue to appeal after their defensive dominance and strong underlying numbers, with David Raya, Riccardo Calafiori, Conor and Saka featuring regularly in elite squads. Calafiori’s advanced positioning, Conor’s ownership surge and Arsenal’s defensive security make a double-up at the back a popular route.

The most common moves in the experts’ team are Bruno Fernandes, Bryan Mbeumo, Harry Maguire and Dominic Calvert-Lewin out, with Palmer, Rogers, Conor and Whiston in. The resulting Gameweek 4 XI is Kinsky; Califiori, Diper and Conor; Rogers, Palmer, Szoboszlai and Gross; Haaland, Whiston and João Pedro, with around £1m spare. Palmer, Rogers, Gross and Conor all carry notably higher ownership among elite managers than in the overall game, while Bruno has a substantial negative expert-ownership gap and is a potential sell for those needing Chelsea attackers. However, some strong managers retain Bruno, believing he offers captaincy potential in Gameweeks 6 and 8 as his ownership falls.

Chip use is unusually aggressive: 25% of the tracked managers have unlimited transfers active, including roughly 20% on Wildcard and 5% on Free Hit, while 7% use Triple Captain. One Wildcard prioritises a more balanced medium-term squad over a one-week Free Hit, pairing Palmer and Rogers with Saka, Mbeumo, Haaland, João Pedro and Barry. The reasoning is to attack Hull while avoiding an excessive Chelsea commitment, retain Saka as a Gameweek 6 captaincy option and exploit Arsenal’s defence. A Free Hit squad, meanwhile, leans fully into Raya, Calafiori, Chelsea’s Palmer-Rogers-João Pedro core, Liverpool’s Szoboszlai and Isak, and attacking defenders such as Diper and Vuskovic. The main caution is that the Triple Captain chip has relatively limited season-long value, so even a Palmer blank is not considered season-defining.

items.title: FPL GW4 Transfer Tips! | Buy, Sell, Keep, Avoid #fpl
items.headline: Cole Palmer becomes the standout Gameweek 4 buy and captaincy gamble against Hull
items.summary:
Cole Palmer is the priority transfer for Gameweek 4 as Chelsea face Hull, with captaincy also a viable aggressive move. Hull remain unbeaten defensively on the surface, but their underlying defensive numbers are among the league’s poorest, suggesting Chelsea’s attacking quality can expose them. João Pedro and Morgan Rogers are also identified as high-priority targets for managers unable to reach Palmer or needing cheaper attacking additions.

Ryan Cherki is the recommended sale after his Manchester City punt against Coventry fails to deliver. City’s influx of attacking signings, combined with a heavier schedule across competitions, makes their midfield and forward options increasingly difficult to trust for starts. Cherki, Phil Foden, Enzo, Nico O’Reilly and other City attackers have quality, but their rotation risk undermines their FPL appeal unless their minutes become more secure.

Dominik Szoboszlai is a firm hold despite blanking in Gameweek 3. He is unfortunate to have two strong efforts saved by Ipswich goalkeeper Shèrpen and a penalty ruled out for a marginal offside, while Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak benefit from goalkeeper errors. Szoboszlai retains reliable minutes, set-piece responsibility, occasional penalty potential and encouraging open-play threat, making him attractive against a leaky Fulham defence.

Managers are advised not to buy Anthony Elanga, Harvey Barnes or, for non-owners, Yoane Wissa this week. Newcastle’s attack is not consistently creating clear-cut chances, and a handful of exceptional individual goals masks underlying overperformance. With Leeds United offering a tougher defensive test, the recommendation is to wait until Gameweek 5, when Newcastle meet Hull, before reassessing their attacking assets.
key_points: Buy Cole Palmer for Chelsea’s Gameweek 4 match against Hull, with captaincy a realistic upside play.
João Pedro and Morgan Rogers are alternative high-priority transfers for managers who cannot reach Palmer.
Sell Ryan Cherki as Manchester City’s growing attacking depth and fixture load make his minutes too uncertain.
Avoid relying on City attackers such as Foden, Enzo and O’Reilly unless there is clearer evidence of secure starts.
Keep Dominik Szoboszlai: he has set pieces, possible penalties, secure minutes and a strong Gameweek 4 fixture against Fulham.
Do not buy Anthony Elanga, Harvey Barnes or Yoane Wissa before Newcastle face Leeds; reassess Newcastle assets for the Gameweek 5 trip to Hull.

items.headline: Milenkovic over White and Konsa is a calculated two-week defensive punt
items.summary:
Nikola Milenkovic replaces Joe Rodon after a weak defence makes a transfer unavoidable. The move is made before Arsenal’s line-up is confirmed, and in hindsight Ben White or Ezri Konsa may have been the safer alternatives.

Milenkovic is backed for Nottingham Forest’s home matches against Newcastle and Crystal Palace, where his clean-sheet potential, defensive-contribution upside and threat from set pieces offer multiple routes to returns. The appeal is not solely dependent on Forest keeping two clean sheets.

The gamble is that Arsenal do not deliver consecutive shutouts. If an Arsenal defender returns a clean sheet in one match but little in the other, a points split such as six and two could be matched by Milenkovic producing steady four-point returns across both fixtures. Konsa and White may look preferable with the benefit of the confirmed information, but Milenkovic is viewed as capable of matching Konsa over the next two gameweeks.

Ben White and Ezri Konsa are acknowledged as possible alternatives, particularly after Arsenal’s line-up becomes clear.

items.headline: Cole Palmer edges Haaland for Gameweek 4 captaincy as FPL squad holds wildcard
items.summary:
Cole Palmer is the preferred captain for Gameweek 4 after Chelsea’s attacking performance in the 6-3 win over Leeds, with João Pedro vice-captain against Hull at Stamford Bridge. Palmer scores twice, takes a penalty and looks sharp alongside Morgan Rogers, who supplies four assists after coming on. Hull are yet to concede in the league, but Chelsea’s home attack appears strong enough to overcome that resistance. Erling Haaland, away to Manchester United, remains a credible alternative but Palmer’s penalty duty, midfielder goal points and clean-sheet point give him the edge.

Three transfers are already confirmed: Bruno Fernandes becomes Palmer, Rodon becomes West Ham defender Konstantinos Mavropanos, and Solanke becomes Morgan Gibbs-White. Palmer is selected over a cheaper Chelsea route such as Rogers because the plan is only for the short stretch before a likely Gameweek 6 wildcard, and the premium midfielder offers the highest explosive upside against Hull and Brentford. Gibbs-White is preferred to Rogers to avoid a triple Chelsea attack and to target Aston Villa away and Coventry at home; he has set pieces, penalties and Forest’s strongest open-play goal threat. However, Rogers’ four-assist display means he now looks a serious alternative and may prove the better short-term pick.

Mavropanos is chosen over Ezri Konsa or Ben White despite the appeal of doubling up on Arsenal’s defence for Sunderland away and Brighton away. The move is made early to avoid Rodon’s price fall and protect squad value before the Arsenal team news is known. Mavropanos has Newcastle and Crystal Palace at home, offers strong defensive-contribution potential and carries some set-piece threat. The risk is clear: Arsenal’s defence looks capable of consecutive clean sheets, but one Mavropanos clean sheet plus defensive points would make the short-term gamble acceptable.

The wildcard is held for Gameweek 6 rather than activated now. A wildcard squad would likely add a second Arsenal defender, replace Dominik Szoboszlai with a stronger Liverpool or midfield option, and possibly move Dominic Calvert-Lewin to Yoane Wissa. But none of those upgrades feels sufficiently decisive over the next two gameweeks to justify using the chip early. Saving it through the international break allows more time for injuries, form and selection patterns to emerge, while a rolled transfer in Gameweek 5 can preserve flexibility.

The starting XI includes Verbruggen over Kinsky in goal, Calafiori and Mavropanos in defence, and Bryan Mbeumo ahead of Gomez despite Mbeumo facing Manchester City. Mbeumo’s form and underlying numbers, including the second-highest expected goals among midfielders, outweigh Gomez’s better Coventry fixture. Haaland, Calvert-Lewin and João Pedro lead the attack, while Szoboszlai stays for Fulham at home and Bournemouth away before the prospective wildcard. The earlier Haaland triple-captain return of nine points is viewed as disappointing but not damaging: the chip’s true lost upside versus ordinary Haaland captaincy is limited, and larger weekly gains can be found through routine selection calls.
key_points: Cole Palmer is the Gameweek 4 captain against Hull, with João Pedro vice-captain and Erling Haaland an alternative away to Manchester United.
Confirmed transfers are Bruno Fernandes to Palmer, Rodon to Konstantinos Mavropanos, and Solanke to Morgan Gibbs-White.
Mavropanos is a short-term punt for Newcastle and Crystal Palace at home, prioritising defensive-contribution and goal threat over an Arsenal defensive double-up.
Gibbs-White gets the nod over Morgan Rogers because of penalties, set pieces, Forest’s fixtures and the desire not to own three Chelsea attackers, although Rogers’ four assists raise doubts.
The wildcard is pencilled in for Gameweek 6 over the international break, with double Arsenal defence and Yoane Wissa among the likely upgrades.
Bryan Mbeumo starts against Manchester City over Gomez against Coventry due to his excellent early-season form and elite expected-goals numbers.
Verbruggen starts over Kinsky, while Calvert-Lewin and Szoboszlai are retained for the next two fixtures before the possible wildcard.

items.title: FPL GW4 EXPERT Wildcard Team & Transfer Trends! 🧠 100 Experts Reveal Gameweek 4 Team Plans
items.headline: Cole Palmer dominates Gameweek 4 plans as experts overhaul squads on Wildcards
items.summary:
Gameweek 4 brings a major expert-led reshuffle, with 35% of the 100 surveyed managers activating a Wildcard and a further 2% using a Free Hit. Only 11% make no move, while most non-chip managers target Chelsea and Arsenal assets. Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa are the overwhelming free-transfer priorities, while Bruno Fernandes, Bryan Mbeumo, Rayan Cherki, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw are among the most common sales ahead of the Manchester derby.

Palmer is the defining pick of the week. He appears in every one of the 35 expert Wildcard drafts and is also captained by 70% of the sample for Chelsea's home fixture against Hull City. João Pedro is the clear fallback captain at 18%, while Erling Haaland receives only 8% backing despite his usual premium appeal. All of the experts using Triple Captain place it on Palmer, although only 4% of the overall group deploy the chip, suggesting many still prefer to save it for a later high-upside week.

The Wildcard template is built around Palmer, Rogers, João Pedro and Haaland, with Riccardo Calafiori and Konsa virtually universal defensive selections at 97% each. Egan-Riley is the preferred £4.0m defender, while Muharemovic and Lewis Hall provide popular additional options. In goal, Kinsky leads the way, ahead of David Raya and Verbruggen, generally paired with a £4.0m reserve. The key Arsenal structure is Calafiori and Konsa plus either Saka or Raya; Saka is marginally more popular, but the Raya-and-Morgan Gibbs-White alternative offers a similarly priced route.

Midfield choices beyond Palmer and Rogers are less settled. Gross is selected in around two-thirds of Wildcards, while Saka, Gibbs-White and Gakpo are viable alternatives. Experts are notably cooler on Gakpo than the wider FPL market: despite being the most-bought player overall, he is included in only 26% of Wildcards, partly because Liverpool's schedule stiffens after Fulham in Gameweek 4. Up front, the third striker slot is the main compromise: Wissa remains the most common choice but falls sharply from his previous near-essential status, with Barry and Gonzalo competing as cheaper alternatives. Bruno Fernandes is in only 9% of Wildcards, underlining the willingness to move away from Manchester United assets for the upcoming fixture swing.
key_points: Cole Palmer is in 100% of expert Wildcards and is the captaincy favourite for Chelsea at home to Hull City, backed by 70% of experts.
Palmer is the only Triple Captain pick in the survey, but just 4% of experts use the chip in Gameweek 4.
Morgan Rogers and Ezri Konsa join Palmer as the standout non-Wildcard transfer targets.
Bruno Fernandes, Bryan Mbeumo, Rayan Cherki, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw are major sales as managers reduce Manchester exposure before the derby.
Riccardo Calafiori and Konsa are selected by 97% of Wildcard teams, with Egan-Riley the preferred budget defender.
João Pedro and Erling Haaland are in 100% and 97% respectively of expert Wildcards; the third forward is split between Wissa, Barry and Gonzalo.

items.title: My transfer tips ahead of Gameweek 4 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: Sell Foden, back Rogers and target Palmer before Gameweek 4
items.summary:
Phil Foden is the priority sale after being benched in Gameweek 3, with Manchester City’s midfield rotation making him too expensive a risk. Rayan Cherki is less urgent to move on because he starts the previous match and faces Manchester United next, a defence that has not looked secure. Even so, Cherki’s long-term minutes remain difficult to trust.

Morgan Rogers is the standout midfield target, with Hull at home next and a favourable enough run beyond that. Bryan Mbeumo is viable either as a hold or a sale to fund Rogers: his minutes remain strong while Amad is unavailable, but managers wanting the Aston Villa midfielder can make the switch. Morgan Gibbs-White is another appealing higher-priced option, particularly with Coventry at home in Gameweek 5 and penalty duties. Bruno Fernandes remains a reliable asset, but moving from Fernandes to Cole Palmer is preferred this week because Palmer offers stronger upside while releasing budget elsewhere.

Thierno Barry is a value forward at £5.6m, with Everton lacking another recognised striker and facing Ipswich at home in Gameweek 5 followed by Hull away in Gameweek 6. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is a reasonable Wildcard sale, but non-Wildcard managers can hold because he has two home matches across the next two Gameweeks and generally secure minutes. In Liverpool’s attack, do not rush to sell Dominik Szoboszlai or Florian Wirtz before Fulham at home. Cody Gakpo looks the best long-term Liverpool forward option due to his ability to play on either wing or through the middle when Alexander Isak is rested. Isak is attractive at £9.1m, but Champions League football is likely to bring more managed minutes and the favourable Ipswich fixture has already passed.

Rayan Cherki can be held for Manchester United next after starting in Gameweek 3, but he is not a dependable long-term minutes pick.
Morgan Rogers is the leading midfield transfer target ahead of Hull at home and a decent fixture run.

items.headline: Cole Palmer edges João Pedro as the Gameweek 4 captaincy call against Hull
items.summary:
Gameweek 4 centres on Chelsea’s home fixture against Hull, with Cole Palmer and João Pedro the standout captaincy options. Hull arrive with clean sheets but have conceded five big chances and rank only 14th for expected goals conceded, having faced low-scoring Villa and Coventry sides. Chelsea’s attack is viewed as a major step up in quality, making a heavy home win plausible. Palmer is preferred to João Pedro for captaincy because of his penalty duties, midfielder scoring and 20-point haul potential, although João Pedro remains close and is considered a near-essential Chelsea attacker.

A Chelsea attacking triple-up is attractive on a Free Hit for Hull at home, with Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers the preferred combination. It is less appealing as a Wildcard structure because Chelsea then face Brentford away, Bournemouth, Everton away and Spurs, while Palmer has not yet established himself as a reliable talisman. Palmer and João Pedro are the recommended longer-term pair. Chelsea’s defence remains difficult to trust after a long clean-sheet drought: Martinez is the only realistic Wildcard option, while Laqua is expensive and Hato, Gusto and Reece James carry rotation or minutes concerns.

Arsenal offer the clearer defensive investment. Ezri Kza, priced at £4.4m, is the leading budget defender after starting ahead of the absent Moscara and delivering both DefCon potential and some attacking involvement. His minutes carry some medium-term risk when competition returns, but Arsenal clean-sheet points alone justify the gamble. Calafiori is seen as close to undroppable when fit, while Raya, Gabriel and Kza make a viable triple defensive Arsenal stack. Bukayo Saka is a good player with penalties while Yarez is absent, but the panel questions whether he is worth the premium over cheaper midfielders and Arsenal defenders; his main value is flexibility to move back to Bruno Fernandes.

Liverpool attackers remain strong Gameweek 4 targets against a struggling Fulham defence. Alexander Isak and Gakpo have upside, but Isak’s managed minutes and injury history make him a risk in a Champions League schedule, while Gakpo has reportedly missed training as a precaution and may face competition for starts. A Free Hit can justify a Liverpool attacking triple-up, but managers without one are advised not to force transfers for them. Erling Haaland remains a safe captain against Manchester United, though João Pedro or Palmer are favoured by some due to Chelsea’s superior fixture.

The transfer theme is restraint. One manager rolls with a viable squad rather than spend another early chip, while another uses a Free Hit to load up on Chelsea, Liverpool and Arsenal. Moving Bruno Fernandes or Bryan Mbeumo out for Chelsea midfielders is not automatically endorsed: Bruno has Fulham next, Mbeumo remains worth starting against Manchester City, and managers should avoid using transfers merely to chase last week’s returns. A Gameweek 6 Wildcard is preferred to an unnecessary Gameweek 4 reset for squads already carrying Palmer, Arsenal coverage and playable forwards.
key_points: Captain Cole Palmer against Hull if chasing Chelsea’s highest ceiling; João Pedro is the main alternative, while Haaland remains the safe pick against Manchester United.
Buy Ezri Kza at £4.4m if a defensive transfer is needed, with Arsenal clean-sheet potential outweighing the future risk from Moscara’s return.
A Wildcard Arsenal triple-up can be Raya, Calafiori and Kza/Gabriel, with the panel preferring defensive certainty to forcing Saka at his premium price.
Use Palmer and João Pedro as the preferred long-term Chelsea pair; reserve a third Chelsea attacker for a Gameweek 4 Free Hit rather than a permanent Wildcard slot.
Avoid Chelsea defenders beyond Martinez unless chasing a short-term punt: Laqua is costly, while Hato, Gusto and Reece James have uncertain minutes.
Liverpool’s Isak and Gakpo are strong Free Hit options against Fulham, but Isak’s fitness management and Gakpo’s training absence make permanent transfer moves less straightforward.
Do not sell Bruno Fernandes or Bryan Mbeumo simply to chase Chelsea assets, especially with Bruno facing Fulham next and Mbeumo still worth starting against City.
Managers with stable squads are encouraged to roll transfers and target a Gameweek 6 Wildcard rather than burn more chips early.

items.headline: Cole Palmer Triple Captain backed for Chelsea’s Gameweek 4 meeting with Hull
items.summary:
A 40-point opening week after the wildcard produces a sharp red arrow, with Trevoh Chalobah’s own goal, yellow cards and widespread blanks compounding the damage. However, the underlying squad structure remains intact and there is no panic over the poor return: the pre-wildcard side also blanks heavily, while the current team retains a strong spread of premium attackers, Arsenal defensive cover and playable bench options.

The Gameweek 4 XI is Raya; Van Hecke, De Cuyper and Konsa; Saka, Foden, Szoboszlai and Gross; Haaland, Wissa and Joao Pedro. Raya is preferred despite his £6.0m price because Arsenal lead the clean-sheet projections at 50%, while Konsa looks increasingly secure for Aston Villa after returning to the starting side. De Cuyper offers attacking upside from set pieces and an advanced role, while Van Hecke remains a reliable cheaper defender. Wissa starts despite a difficult trip to Leeds because none of the bench options is more appealing.

The decisive move is Foden to Cole Palmer, funded by £3.3m in the bank, with Palmer handed the triple-captain armband for Chelsea at home to Hull. Manchester City attackers are considered too difficult to trust beyond Haaland because rotation is likely, while Palmer has the week’s best projected goal total in a fixture that looks better than Hull’s three opening clean sheets suggest. Hull have conceded more than five expected goals, the 13th-worst record in the league, so their defensive record is viewed as unsustainable. Joao Pedro becomes vice-captain, while Haaland remains a perfectly viable ordinary captain against Manchester United given his eight goals and three assists in seven derbies.

The chip call also reflects doubts over later triple-captain alternatives. Haaland at home to Ipswich in Gameweek 7 carries a potential rotation concern after Liverpool and PSG, while Bruno Fernandes at home to Coventry in Gameweek 14 depends on Manchester United improving and surviving the Champions League schedule. The plan is to roll transfers in Gameweeks 5 and 6, then potentially replace De Cuyper in Gameweek 7 with Bournemouth’s Marcos Senesi if minutes become uncertain. Longer term, a Gameweek 8 move away from Haaland is under consideration, freeing funds to build a midfield around Palmer, Saka, Bruno Fernandes and other penalty-taking assets, but Haaland is retained for now.
key_points: Transfer Foden out for Cole Palmer in Gameweek 4, using £3.3m in the bank.
Triple-captain Palmer against Hull, with Joao Pedro as vice-captain.
Haaland is a strong standard captain option against Manchester United but is not preferred over Palmer’s home fixture.
Raya, Konsa and Arsenal’s clean-sheet projection support retaining expensive Arsenal defensive cover.
Hull’s three clean sheets are viewed as unsustainable after conceding more than five expected goals in three matches.
Plan to roll transfers in Gameweeks 5 and 6 unless De Cuyper’s minutes become a concern.
A potential Gameweek 7 defensive switch is De Cuyper to Bournemouth’s Marcos Senesi, whose favourable run begins with Sunderland at home.
A longer-term Haaland exit around Gameweek 8 could fund a premium midfield featuring Palmer, Saka and Bruno Fernandes.

items.headline: Saka offers Arsenal upside, but triple defence remains the Wildcard safety play
items.summary:
Arsenal’s defensive strength makes a double-up feel close to essential on a Wildcard, with Riccardo Calafiori and Ezri Konsa presented as the standout value routes. Calafiori is effectively playing with the attacking licence of a midfielder, having already had a Gameweek 3 goal ruled out, so his appeal does not rely solely on clean sheets. Konsa’s £4.4m price makes him an extremely cheap way into the Arsenal back line.

The main Wildcard decision is the third Arsenal slot. David Raya offers the safest route: a reliable stream of clean sheets with occasional save points, alongside Calafiori and Konsa. The concern is whether Raya at £6.0m is worth the premium over a £4.5m goalkeeper such as Bart Verbruggen, while Gabriel at £8.0m is difficult to accommodate.

A more aggressive structure is double Arsenal defence plus one attacker, with Bukayo Saka the preferred high-ceiling option. Saka has scored in the opening gameweeks, carries potential penalty responsibility depending on the line-up, and offers the explosive returns that a third defender cannot match. Martin Odegaard is also attracting interest after returning to form at a relatively affordable price, while William Saliba improves in Gameweek 3 after an underwhelming Gameweek 2 and remains another defensive consideration.

Saka’s price is also useful for squad flexibility: if he fails to justify the investment, he can be downgraded easily to almost any midfield alternative, including a route back to Bruno Fernandes. The lean is currently Calafiori, Konsa and Saka, balancing Arsenal’s defensive security with attacking upside. The alternative is to lock in triple Arsenal defence, avoid future selection headaches and potentially hold the unit for much of the season, but that comes at the cost of access to a crowded pool of strong attackers.
key_points: Riccardo Calafiori and Ezri Konsa are viewed as near-lock Wildcard picks for a double Arsenal defensive investment.
Calafiori offers attacking upside beyond clean sheets, having had a goal disallowed in Gameweek 3 despite early substitutions.
David Raya is the safest third Arsenal pick, but his £6.0m cost is questioned against £4.5m options such as Bart Verbruggen.
Bukayo Saka is the preferred third Arsenal slot for managers chasing upside, with early goals, potential penalties and a high ceiling.
Saka’s price makes future moves easy, as he can be downgraded to most midfielders or used to return to Bruno Fernandes.
Triple Arsenal defence is the conservative route and could be held long term, but it limits access to other strong attacking options.

items.headline: Isak and Gakpo emerge as Liverpool’s best Fulham punts in Gameweek 4
items.summary:
Liverpool’s home match against Fulham in Gameweek 4 stands out as one of the strongest alternatives to the Chelsea-Haaland fixture. Fulham concede heavily early in the season and are viewed as one of the league’s weakest defences, making this an attractive one-week entry point for Liverpool attackers.

Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo are preferred over Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz on both the eye test and underlying data. Liverpool are expected to keep creating high-quality chances under Andoni Iraola’s attacking approach, as his Bournemouth teams do, but Isak and Gakpo currently look like the most convincing routes into those chances. Gakpo appears relatively secure for minutes, while Isak is the standout target for managers buying now or activating a Wildcard.

The main caution is Liverpool’s fixture swing immediately after Fulham. Their run includes Bournemouth, Manchester City, Brentford, Brighton and Arsenal, with Arsenal leading the league for expected goals conceded, City second and Brentford also posting strong defensive numbers. Brighton looks a potentially exploitable fixture, but the overall schedule is not strong enough to make Liverpool attackers automatic long-term holds.

Managers who already own Szoboszlai may reasonably keep him, particularly because of his reliable minutes and possible penalty involvement, rather than using a transfer or chip to chase another Liverpool option. For new buyers, however, Gameweek 4 is the time to act: Isak is the preferred signing, Gakpo is a viable alternative, and managers who pass on Liverpool this week may be better served looking elsewhere unless they are building a Haaland-free squad.
key_points: Liverpool at home to Fulham in Gameweek 4 is a prime attacking fixture because Fulham are among the weakest defences so far.
Alexander Isak is the preferred Liverpool buy for managers making a transfer or playing a Wildcard.
Cody Gakpo is also an appealing option, with strong recent performances and relatively secure minutes.
Dominik Szoboszlai remains a reasonable hold for current owners due to his minutes and potential penalty duty.
Liverpool’s fixtures worsen after Fulham, with Manchester City, Brentford and Arsenal all presenting difficult defensive opposition.
Managers buying a Liverpool attacker should view Gameweek 4 as the key entry point rather than a long-term fixture run.
